chunks: And among them is al-Mu'alla ibn Khunais, and he was one of the servants (or stewards) of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and it was because of him that Dawud ibn Ali had him killed. He was praised by him, and he proceeded upon his path/method, and his affair/status is well-known.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, title of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.المُعَلَّى بْنُ خُنَيْسٍ: al-Mu'alla ibn Khunais, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.دَاوُدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Dawud ibn Ali, a Umayyad governor
key_terms.قَوَامِ: servants, stewards, or those in charge of affairs
key_terms.مَنْهَاجِهِ: his path or method (of religious practice)

ai.seo_question: Who was al-Mu'alla ibn Khunais and why was he killed?
ai.summary: Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunais is identified as one of the 'Qawam' (trusted deputies) of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, a role signifying high authority in transmitting hadith and managing communal affairs during the Minor Occultation's precursor era. His martyrdom by Dawud ibn Ali underscores the political tensions of the Umayyad period, while his designation as 'Mahmud' (praised) and 'Mushahir' (famous) reflects his enduring status as a reliable narrator in Shia hadith sciences.
